blind_spots: Validates the computational runner only — does not exercise the inferential runner's blocking-rejection (which is structurally similar but has its own copy of the check; see skills/run-sensor/scripts/run-inferential.go).

The originating UseCase .harness/usecases/run-sensor-blocking-rejected.json claims exit_code=1 and a verdict=error Signal envelope; the implementation emits exit_code=2 + plain stderr instead. This sensor asserts the implementation's truth.
Substring grep for 'blocking' and 'start-sensor' tolerates wording changes (e.g. capitalization). A reworded remediation that omits either keyword would silently flip the verdict to fail.

The sensor's command shells out via `go run` (not a precompiled binary), and `go run` wraps the runner's exit code: the runner exits 2 on rejection, but the outer `go run` wrapper exits 1 while echoing 'exit status 2' to stderr. To stay robust to both invocation modes (wrapped and direct), the command treats any non-zero rc as acceptable as long as stderr carries both keywords.
description: Asserts that invoking the run-computational runner with a sensor whose execution.blocking=true short-circuits before any subprocess is spawned, exits 2, and prints a stderr message naming both 'blocking' and 'start-sensor' so the calling agent can remediate. Authored via /create-sensor from .harness/usecases/run-sensor-blocking-rejected.json; validates the actual implementation at skills/run-sensor/scripts/run-computational.go (the UseCase's claimed exit_code=1 and Signal-envelope output do not match the implementation — the truth is exit_code=2 + plain stderr).

execution.command: set -u; F="${HARNESS_REGISTRY_ROOT}/.harness/sensors/fixtures/assert-run-sensor-rejects-blocking/blocking-fixture.json"; out=$(GOWORK=off HARNESS_REGISTRY_ROOT="${HARNESS_REGISTRY_ROOT}" go run -C "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}" -tags=run_computational ./skills/run-sensor/scripts "${F}" 2>&1); rc=$?; if [ "${rc}" -ne 0 ] && printf '%s' "${out}" | grep -q 'blocking' && printf '%s' "${out}" | grep -q 'start-sensor'; then exit 0; else printf 'expected non-zero rc + output containing both "blocking" and "start-sensor"; got rc=%s out=%s\n' "${rc}" "${out}" >&2; exit 1; fi

name: /run-sensor refuses to spawn a blocking sensor

requires.description: Absolute path of the harness-framework plugin checkout. The sensor's command uses `go run -C` to ensure module resolution happens inside the plugin tree regardless of the project's cwd or go.work.

requires.description: Absolute path of the user project root. Captured before go -C chdirs the toolchain so the fixture path the sensor's command points at resolves correctly.
